speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy having trouble feeding and your tummy looks swollen. Can you tell me if you are vomiting, and if so, does it look like yellow bile or green fluid? Also, how is your gas passing?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like significant pain; has your baby been passing any gas, or have you noticed any episodes of projectile vomiting, especially if it appears green? Also, has he had any bowel movements in the last 24 hours?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception. The clinical picture of an 8-month-old with progressive abdominal distension, tenderness (crying on touch), and a history of normal birth is highly suggestive of this condition, even in the absence of projectile vomiting or fever at this stage. I need to visualize the bowel immediately. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound.
